page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, providing a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a 35 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.n2.large sits in the lower performance tiers for modern workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. Memory read bandwidth is also limited, registering in the bottom 25%, though large-block memory write bandwidth achieves average tier results. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 operations, show poor performance, falling into the bottom 10% of tested systems.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.n2.large is its modest processing throughput and lack of bundled local storage, which requires reliance on external block storage. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution times compared to burstable instances, making it a stable option for resource-constrained workloads. This instance is best utilized for general-purpose tasks such as lightweight web serving, development environments, basic database operations, and low-throughput background processing.
